title: Now May Fervent Prayer Arise
description: Now May Fervent Prayer Arise in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 9, “Prayer for a blessing”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now may fer-vent prayer a-rise Winged with faith, and pierce the skies; Fer-vent prayer shall bring us down Gra-cious an-swers from the throne.

lines: Now may fervent prayer arise
Winged with faith, and pierce the skies;
Fervent prayer shall bring us down
Gracious answers from the throne.
Bless, O Lord, the op'ning year
To each soul assembled here;
Clothe thy word with pow'r divine,
Make us willing to be thine.
Shepherd of thy blood-bought sheep!
Teach the stony heart to weep;
Let the blind have eyes to see,
See themselves, and look on thee!
Let the minds of all our youth
Feel the force of sacred truth;
While the gospel-call they hear
May they learn to love and fear!
Show them what their ways have been,
Show them the desert of sin;
Then thy dying love reveal,
This shall melt a heart of steel.
Where thou hast thy work begun,
Give new strength the race to run;
Scatter darkness, doubts and fears,
Wipe away the mourners tears.
Bless us all, both old and young;
Call forth praise from every tongue;
Let the whole assembly prove
All thy pow'r, and all thy love!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
